key_insight: Spherical propeller forcing produces a purely forward energy cascade across the investigated scales, even though energy flux retains directional dependence.
engineering_relevance: The proposed framework links propeller frequency to key turbulence variables, supporting the design and tuning of nearly homogeneous, isotropic turbulence chambers.
method: Apply the Kármán–Howarth–Monin framework to scale-by-scale energy transfer without assuming isotropy.
Analyze Eulerian temporal statistics under low mean flow, where Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis does not apply.
Relate measured turbulence variables to propeller frequency and compare with previously reported HIT chambers.
evidence_signal: Experiments show orientation-averaged structure functions consistent with Kolmogorov’s two-thirds law and intermediate-scale temporal statistics supporting Tennekes’ Eulerian frequency spectrum.
watch_item: Nearly isotropic energy distributions do not guarantee isotropic energy flux; residual forcing asymmetries may still affect transfer directionality.
paper_title: Interscale energy transfer in a propeller-driven homogeneous and isotropic turbulence generation device
